images.title: The center projects forward
images.caption: The advancing Iberian and Celtic center stands ahead of the African infantry on the wings. The first contact will come in the middle.
images.prompt: Create a single photorealistic, landscape-format historical reenactment still. Natural color as if professionally photographed on location; human, restrained, materially credible, candid composition. No captions, letters, maps, labels, watermark, collage or painted surface. Cannae, Apulia, second Punic War, summer 216 BCE. Wide cinematic high oblique view from above one end of Hannibal’s line, looking along it. On an open dry river plain the long, relatively thin Iberian and Celtic infantry center bows outward in a broad shallow convex arc TOWARD a dense approaching Roman infantry block. The heavy African foot stand farther back at the shoulders. Human texture in nearest files: Iberian light short tunics with restrained dark purple edging, long shields; groups with varied dress beside them. Bronze and iron, tan fields, hazy low hills. A naturalistic museum reconstruction, army-level depth and distinct opposing formations. No icons, letters, elephants, flags, medieval or imperial gear, parade geometry, cauldron, or perfect ring.

images.title: Pressure on the Roman rear
images.caption: As African infantry turns against the flanks, Hasdrubal’s horsemen attack the Roman infantry from behind. This view follows one local attack.
